title: Criterion-related validity of the Borg ratings of perceived exertion scale in healthy individuals: a meta-analysis
authors: Chen MJ, Fan X, Moe ST
population: Healthy individuals in studies correlating Borg RPE with physiological criterion measures
findings: Weighted mean validity coefficients between RPE and physiological criteria were 0.62 for heart rate, 0.57 for blood lactate, 0.64 for %VO2max, 0.63 for VO2, 0.61 for ventilation and 0.72 for respiration rate.
Moderators: for heart rate, fitness, type of exercise, protocol and RPE mode; for lactate, sex and RPE scale; for VO2, sex, exercise type and RPE mode.

Highest correlations occurred in specific conditions, e.g. males exerting maximally, unusual exercise tasks such as swimming (rather than walking or running for HR, %VO2max and VO2), or the 15-point scale for lactate.
Authors conclude Borg RPE is a valid measure of exercise intensity but its validity may be lower than previously thought (r = 0.80-0.90), except under certain conditions.
limitations: Pre-2002 studies pooled across many protocols; the abstract gives no study or participant counts; covers Borg scales in general, not session-RPE, CR-10 or runners specifically.
implications: Do not treat RPE as a precise physiological measurement: the pooled correlation with heart rate is about 0.62, so the engine should not auto-correct sRPE from HR (or the reverse) when they disagree.

When both sRPE and HR load exist for a session, keep both and surface divergence as information, not error. Any flag threshold (for example a difference in within-user z-scores) is a design choice, not from this paper.

verification.notes: Crossref confirms title, J Sports Sci, 2002, first author Chen. Abstract read in Europe PMC; all coefficients match. Added the VO2 moderators and the walking/running qualifier that the researcher omitted.
